section_map.section: Searching for a Lost Plane abstract
section_map.summary: Input: A transoceanic flight beyond coastal radar, a last communication on the intended path, sparse prior evidence, and finite search resources. Analytical job: Name the casualty-distance density, glide/deviation field, POC cells, Koopman POD, nondetection update, neighborhood search, Flight ABCD example, sensitivity, and strengths. Output: A conditional promise that a source-parameterized, continuously updated neighborhood plan can prioritize a bounded search region. Handoff: The contents and introduction unpack the observation gap, model stages, evaluation, worked example, communication artifact, and code.

Input: The abstract's containment-detection-search promise. Analytical job: Order Introduction; containment, discretization, coordinates, POD, updating, assumptions, sensitivity, evaluation; Flight ABCD; conclusion; press summary; Appendices A-D. Output: A source-heading map that keeps each model interface and evidence artifact distinct. Handoff: The Introduction supplies the offshore observation problem and sparse-prior motivation.

Input: Eighty-three vanished aircraft, limited offshore radar, scheduled pilot communication, and contrasting Air France/MH370 evidence histories. Analytical job: Connect radar loss to communication triggers; contrast informative versus sparse priors; require indefinite casualty timing, deviation from the IFP, no signal, and time efficiency. Output: A sparse-prior missing-flight search objective with explicit trajectory and time priorities. Handoff: The model overview decomposes that objective into containment, detection, and iterative priority updates.

Input: A flight traveling linearly from A to B whose location and detectability are unknown after last contact. Analytical job: Separate containment, conditional detection under resource conservation, and continuously updated most-likely location. Output: A containment -> detection -> updating decomposition for an optimized search plan. Handoff: Section 2.1 first constructs the spatial probability field.

section_map.section: 2.1 Constructing Probabilities of Containment for a Missing Airplane and its Debris
section_map.summary: Input: Last-contact distance and coordinates, remaining route to coastal radar, aircraft altitude and glide ratio, and possible lateral deviation. Analytical job: Define a decreasing quadratic casualty-distance density; compute radar horizon; translate by Gh; model cross-track position normally with sigma_x=Gh sin(pi/8); multiply independent marginals. Output: A bounded along-track and normal cross-track joint density f(x,Y_I). Handoff: Discretization integrates this continuous density into region-level probabilities of containment.

section_map.section: 2.1.1 Partitioning Search Region Through Model Discretization
section_map.summary: Input: The joint density, three-sigma cross-track support, search-plane speed, and a half-hour cell traversal target. Analytical job: Bound x at three standard deviations; choose N by along-track span divided by 0.5 v_s; divide into N by 6 cells; exploit symmetry; integrate each cell in Mathematica. Output: A source-ordered list of POC values assigned to an N by 6 search-region matrix. Handoff: Coordinate transformation converts each selected cell from IFP-relative miles to latitude and longitude.

section_map.section: 2.1.2 Finding Latitude and Longitude Coordinates for Search Regions
section_map.summary: Input: Integer cell indices, sigma_x, the along-track partition, y0 and yB in local and geographic systems, and the flight-vector components. Analytical job: Assemble corner matrix C; infer orientation phi; choose the sign-specific rotation R; check det(R)=1; scale and translate to C_L. Output: Latitude-longitude coordinates for every bounding corner of a selected region. Handoff: POD next quantifies whether search assets can detect the target while traversing such a region.

Input: One cell's area, effective detection distance, search altitude, condition factor, swept distance, synchronized aircraft count, and parallel-swath geometry. Analytical job: Adapt Koopman's exponential; compute A_S, projected detection reach, sweep width S, distance per swath d_s, effort d_s n, and final POD. Output: A region-level POD that can be uniform when search effort does not vary by region. Handoff: Nondetection uses POD to update the searched region's POC.

section_map.section: 2.3 The POC-Updating Algorithm / 2.3.1 Using the POC-Updating Algorithm to Determine Search Pattern
section_map.summary: Input: An N by 6 POC matrix, region-specific POD, the just-searched cell, and its adjacent neighbors. Analytical job: Retain POC_q(1-POD_q) in the searched cell; spread removed mass across other cells; compare updated adjacent POCs; choose the highest neighbor to reduce nonadjacent travel. Output: An iterative POC map and local next-region sequence that permits later revisits. Handoff: The assumption list defines when the distribution, detector, and path sequence are intended to apply.

Input: The complete containment, detection, and search-pattern chain. Analytical job: Fix a linear route, glide-before-impact, water-impact breakup, three-sigma deviation, stationary debris, constant speeds, near-contact prior, persistent detectability, and homogeneous search aircraft. Output: A nine-item operating contract for the model and worked example. Handoff: Sensitivity analysis varies selected parameters inside this contract.

Input: The joint density and POD equations plus G, deviation angle theta, search altitude h_s, effective range, condition factor, and search-plane count n. Analytical job: Plot density response to G/theta; plot POD(theta), POD(G), POD(h_s), and POD(n); state the h_s < kappa epsilon feasibility condition; interpret accommodation versus robustness. Output: A directional parameter-to-response map and an explicit sensor-reach feasibility boundary. Handoff: Strengths and weaknesses evaluate the mechanisms revealed by the construction and sensitivity pass.

section_map.section: 2.6 Strengths and Weaknesses of Our Model / 2.6.1 Strengths / 2.6.2 Weaknesses
section_map.summary: Input: The nonuniform prior, trajectory mapping, coordinate transform, condition-adjusted POD, updating rule, neighborhood restriction, and assumption set. Analytical job: Contrast the quadratic prior with uniform time; credit trajectory and coordinate conversion; explain kappa and updating; identify cross-track allocation distortion and omitted currents. Output: A mechanism-specific capability and boundary record plus two repair targets. Handoff: Flight ABCD demonstrates how the retained mechanisms connect numerically.

section_map.section: 3 Working Example: Flight ABCD to Lisbon, Portugal Reported Missing
section_map.summary: Input: Boston-Lisbon endpoints, last-contact coordinates, B777 speed/altitude/glide ratio, search-plane speed/altitude/instrument, kappa=0.98, and eight aircraft. Analytical job: Instantiate f_YC, f_YI, f(x), and f(x,Y_I); integrate 36 POCs; calculate POD=0.677831; generate adjacent and unrestricted paths; transform one cell to latitude-longitude corners. Output: A complete scenario record with probability surfaces, cell matrix/map, search path, comparator, and operational coordinates. Handoff: The conclusion generalizes the resource and neighborhood lessons while retaining the currents gap.

Input: Flight ABCD results, sensitivity relationships, fleet-size effect, neighborhood path comparison, and the omitted-current limitation. Analytical job: Emphasize parameterized aircraft/search assets, increased detection with more planes, local travel reduction, and future current/debris modeling. Output: A neighborhood-search recommendation conditioned on careful resource selection and an explicit drift extension. Handoff: The press-conference summary translates the same route for a nontechnical audience.

section_map.section: 5 Summary for an Airline's Press Conference
section_map.summary: Input: Public concern about MH370 and the paper's last-contact-to-neighborhood-search method. Analytical job: Explain search-region narrowing, glide-based impact prediction, POC, POD and added parties, miss-driven next-neighbor selection, revisits, straight-path difficulty, and assumptions. Output: A public-facing explanation of prediction, detection, iterative search, resource adjustment, and restricted applicability. Handoff: References and appendices expose the external evidence and computational artifacts behind the explanation.

Input: Claims about glide, search theory, radar coverage, missing-aircraft prevalence, and Air France/MH370 evidence. Analytical job: Map six citations to flight physics, Koopman/search theory, radar range, missing-aircraft context, and incident comparison. Output: A concise provenance map whose external bytes and calibration datasets are not frozen with the paper. Handoff: Appendices expose the authors' own integration, transform, update, and path-generation artifacts.

section_map.section: 6 Appendix A / 7 Appendix B / 8 Appendix C / 9 Appendix D
section_map.summary: Input: The declared formulas, Flight ABCD parameters, region POCs, coordinate conversion, and two search-pattern variants. Analytical job: Show regional integration loops, Excel coordinate tables, parameter/POC initialization, POD code, miss updates, local/global minimum selection, tie handling, and printed region sequences. Output: Partial reproduction artifacts for the POC grid, coordinate handoff, adjacent path, and nonadjacent comparator. Handoff: The document terminates after program output; no later section resolves code, notation, or reproducibility gaps.

assumptions.summary: The missing aircraft follows a linear pre-established route from A to B.
The aircraft glides into the ocean and does not explode before water impact.
Cross-track deviation remains within three times Gh sin(pi/8).
Currents and other forces do not move the aircraft or debris after impact.
Lost and search aircraft maintain constant velocities.
The aircraft is more likely to lie near the last communication point.
The aircraft remains afloat and detectable throughout the search.
All search aircraft share instrumentation, speed, and altitude.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Missing-aircraft counts and Air France/MH370 narratives motivate the sparse-evidence domain but are not a calibrated incident population.
Last-contact distance, remaining route, coastal radar geometry, altitude, and glide ratio are converted into along-track variables.
A fixed pi/8 deviation scale and independence assumption extend the along-track distribution into a joint surface.
Search speed and a 0.5-hour traversal target determine N; three cross-track sigma bands on either side produce an N by 6 grid.
Cell indices, endpoint coordinates, flight-vector components, rotation, and a mile-degree factor feed the geographic handoff.
Sensor range, weather-condition factor, search altitude, swath distance, and aircraft count parameterize POD.
Flight ABCD fixes Boston-Lisbon geometry, last contact at 40.9275 N and 46.2575 W, y_B=1912 miles, speed 560 mph, altitude 7.58 miles, y_R=199.86, and G=19.
The worked search uses v_s=550 mph, t_0.5=0.5 h, epsilon=4 miles, kappa=0.98, h_s=2000/5280 miles, and n=8 aircraft.

models.summary: Convert last contact, remaining route, radar horizon, and aircraft glide into an along-track impact-distance density.
Extend the one-dimensional impact distance across the ocean surface and create the continuous POC field.
Partition the continuous joint density into finite cells whose traversal length matches half an hour of search-plane travel.
Convert selected probability-cell corners from IFP-relative miles into latitude-longitude coordinates for search deployment.
Compute region-level POD from cell geometry, projected instrument reach, search conditions, altitude, swept distance, and aircraft count.
Reduce the searched cell after nondetection and preserve the source's constant total POC by redistributing removed mass.
Choose a high-POC adjacent cell after each miss to reduce travel time and fuel relative to unrestricted probability chasing.
Trace how glide, deviation, search altitude, instrument range/conditions, and aircraft count affect containment, detection, and feasibility.
Instantiate the containment chain for a Boston-to-Lisbon Boeing 777 and calculate the joint field and regional POCs.
Apply the detector, update/path algorithms, adjacency comparison, and local-to-geographic transform to Flight ABCD.
Synthesize the worked example, fleet sensitivity, neighborhood mechanism, restrictions, and future current/debris work into technical and public recommendations.

results_trace.summary: Flight ABCD sets y_B=1912 miles, speed 560 mph, altitude 7.58 miles, y_R=199.86 miles, and glide ratio G=19 from the Boston-Lisbon scenario.
The source prints casualty support 0<=y_C<1712.14 and impact support 144.02<=y_I<1712.14, with the latter retained as a flagged transformation boundary.
The instantiated joint surface is integrated into 36 search regions (N=6 along-track by six cross-track bands).
Figures 10-11 present the numerical POC grid and map; Appendix C begins with symmetric near-track values including 0.13367 in the first along-track band.
With v_s=550, epsilon=4, kappa=0.98, h_s=2000/5280, and eight search aircraft, the paper reports POD=0.677831.
The neighborhood algorithm produces a locally adjacent sequence and allows revisits after nondetection updates.
The unrestricted comparator visibly alternates across the symmetric IFP more often; the paper reports greater travel qualitatively but supplies no distance or fuel total.
For the sigma,N=2-to-3 region, the source reports phi=-0.057939 and a displayed 2 by 2 rotation with coefficients about 0.9983 and 0.0579 before listing geographic corners.
The conclusion recommends the neighborhood method with careful resource selection and more aircraft, while retaining currents and debris motion as future work.
The press summary translates POC, POD, missed-detection revisits, neighborhood movement, and straight-route restrictions into public chronology.

contributions.summary: Containment, detection, and miss-driven updating are separated before formulas, preserving distinct probability roles.
Last contact, radar horizon, and glide translate sparse flight evidence into a bounded along-track distribution.
Cross-track uncertainty and discretization convert a continuous surface into half-hour operational cells.
A rotation-and-translation interface connects local probability cells to latitude-longitude deployment coordinates.
The POD layer exposes sensor reach, conditions, altitude, swath distance, and fleet size as decision parameters.
Nondetection retains residual probability and enables revisits rather than treating a searched cell as empty.
The worked example compares travel-aware neighborhood selection with unrestricted probability chasing.
A public summary carries the technical sequence and restrictions into stakeholder communication.

writing_logic.summary: abstract: Preview the complete model as a positive construction from containment through detection and updating before assumptions and transfer limits. The contents and introduction unpack the observation gap, model stages, evaluation, worked example, communication artifact, and code.

title: Make the entire analytical route visible, including sensitivity, limitations, public communication, and computational appendices. The Introduction supplies the offshore observation problem and sparse-prior motivation.

introduction: Establish why a new search model is needed when familiar Bayesian elimination lacks strong incident-specific priors. The model overview decomposes that objective into containment, detection, and iterative priority updates.
problem-analysis: Give the reader a three-part interface before any probability density or algorithm is introduced. Section 2.1 first constructs the spatial probability field.

model-establishment: Turn physical narrative into a traceable joint impact-location distribution rather than asserting a search region. Discretization integrates this continuous density into region-level probabilities of containment.

algorithm: Make a continuous location prior actionable as a finite matrix with a time interpretation. Coordinate transformation converts each selected cell from IFP-relative miles to latitude and longitude.

data-preprocessing: Close the gap between a mathematical grid and coordinates a search-and-rescue team can receive. POD next quantifies whether search assets can detect the target while traversing such a region.

model-improvement: Retain containment and detection as separate probabilities and make resource/scenario changes enter through named parameters. Nondetection uses POD to update the searched region's POC.

robustness-verification: Connect imperfect sensing to the next operational action rather than treating one unsuccessful pass as elimination. The assumption list defines when the distribution, detector, and path sequence are intended to apply.
assumptions: Expose physical and resource idealizations before sensitivity or claims of transfer. Sensitivity analysis varies selected parameters inside this contract.

sensitivity-robustness: Show which inputs control probability concentration, detectability, feasibility, and resource response. Strengths and weaknesses evaluate the mechanisms revealed by the construction and sensitivity pass.

strengths-limitations: Attribute reuse value to concrete mechanisms and name omissions without allowing criticism to replace the positive chain. Flight ABCD demonstrates how the retained mechanisms connect numerically.
results: Demonstrate that the model is an end-to-end procedure rather than disconnected formulas. The conclusion generalizes the resource and neighborhood lessons while retaining the currents gap.
conclusion: Return the technical chain to time efficiency, resource choice, and a bounded search recommendation. The press-conference summary translates the same route for a nontechnical audience.

memo: Translate the full technical workflow into chronological operations and a small set of understandable restrictions. References and appendices expose the external evidence and computational artifacts behind the explanation.
references: Expose the external basis of major model choices and contextual claims. Appendices expose the authors' own integration, transform, update, and path-generation artifacts.

appendix: Expose enough computational structure to audit interfaces and outputs even though a fully executable archive is absent. The document terminates after program output; no later section resolves code, notation, or reproducibility gaps.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The abstract previews containment, detection, updating, sensitivity, worked example, and strengths as one operational chain; award status does not prove which move caused judging success.
A density-to-grid-to-map sequence lets a judge inspect how probability becomes an actionable region rather than only seeing formulas.

weaknesses.summary: The printed CDF derivation retains squared terms and dy_C in its alleged antiderivative. Preserve the source form as evidence only and re-derive the integral before numeric reuse.
The translated impact variable Y_I=Y_C+Gh should shift both support limits, but the printed upper support remains y_B-y_R rather than y_B-y_R+Gh.
The joint density inherits the impact-density support inconsistency, so its normalization and every downstream regional integral require a corrected support audit.
The printed indexed x inequality is not an unambiguous lower-and-upper cell-bound contract; the role and sign of l must be made explicit before generating corners.
The printed y bound uses y_B-y_0-Gh and does not clearly preserve the earlier radar-horizon and impact-support terms, creating a geometry mismatch between density, partition, and coordinates.
rho is described as miles per degree but is multiplied in C_L=rho R C+y_0. A miles-to-degrees transform normally requires the reciprocal convention, so units and direction must be reconciled.

Multiplying the searched-cell POC by 1-POD is a likelihood step, but the subsequent uniform mass redistribution is a mass-conserving heuristic rather than a normalized Bayesian posterior conditioned on nondetection.
Selecting the largest updated adjacent POC reduces some travel relative to unrestricted probability chasing, but no global time, fuel, coverage, or detection-optimality proof is supplied.
Separate one-at-a-time curves for G and theta do not establish the prose claim about the combined quantity G+theta; joint interactions and parameter domains are not tested.
The altitude discussion refers to Figure 4 while the relevant plot is Figure 7, so figure-to-claim traceability is broken at the point of sensitivity interpretation.

The prose says POD increases with search altitude, but the plotted curve and square-root detector term decrease as altitude approaches effective instrument reach; the later low-altitude recommendation contradicts the first sentence.
Figure 8 varies search-plane count n but its caption labels the curve POD(h_s), so the displayed independent variable must be recovered from axes and surrounding prose.
Flight ABCD's numerical impact-density center and support do not transparently follow the general Y_I=Y_C+Gh translation, and no normalization or substitution audit is shown.
The methodology defines the condition factor as kappa, but the worked-example and Appendix C POD expression use k; the executable code must bind one symbol explicitly.
Appendix A integrates y_I from zero-based partition bounds and does not visibly add the Gh offset used by the impact variable, so its 36 POC values may not represent the declared density support.
Appendices C and D apply Ceiling to a probability-matrix redistribution term. Integer rounding is incompatible with fractional POC conservation and may collapse or inflate the update.

The Mathematica While conditions are separated by semicolons, and local 3x3 minima are matched through a global Position call. Loop termination, index safety, and selected-cell locality are not executable without clarification.

Appendix C is introduced as the neighborhood algorithm in the body but its page-28 heading says the loop is without adjacency, conflicting with the local 3x3 selection intended to distinguish it from Appendix D.
The conclusion claims applicability to all aircraft and search-plane types from one hypothetical Boeing 777 scenario with uncalibrated sensing and no field comparator.

Claims that the plan is valid, maximizes resources, is a breakthrough, and will be implemented are not supported by optimization certificates, calibrated data, field validation, or deployment evidence.

Fit cross-track deviation and dependence from incident or simulator data, then normalize the corrected joint density on a geodesic support.
Choose adaptive cells by probability mass, sensor footprint, turn cost, terrain/ocean constraints, and computation instead of a fixed half-hour N by 6 grid.
Replace the local flat rotation with a documented geodesic coordinate library, typed miles/degrees units, corner tests, and round-trip validation.
Calibrate the observation likelihood using aircraft/debris signature, sea state, weather, altitude, sensor mode, dwell time, operator performance, and false alarms.
Use a normalized Bayesian filter for missed detections and propagate spatial drift through currents, debris separation, and time-varying detectability.
Optimize multi-aircraft routes over posterior mass, travel, turns, fuel, refueling, separation, coordination, revisit value, and stopping criteria; compare against the greedy neighborhood rule.
Publish a deterministic reproduction package with corrected formulas, exact cell matrix, Mathematica/Excel versions, seeds, tests, raw paths, travel totals, and coordinate fixtures.
